title: Assassination Of Wang Wei San, Journalist At Nanking

page_data.en:
Fm. 2
G. 35m-11432

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 4461
Special Branch 273
REPORT
Date February 3, 1933.

Subject (in full) Attached newspaper cutting

Made by Supt. Tan Shao-liang Forwarded by Tho Robertson, Supt

According to information received from Nanking,
Wang Wei San, the Nanking correspondent of the China
Times (Shanghai) was murdered at 4 p.m. January 31
somewhere near the Ming Tomb, Nanking two men who
according to an eye witness were both dressed in foreign
clothes, age about 20 who looked like students. Motive
of crime is still unknown. The Nanking Authorities will
offer a reward for the arrest of the murderers.

The deceased was a noted journalist, and old
member of the Kuomintang, having served in the various
newspaper offices for twenty years. He was a native of
Anhwei, age 52. He left a widow and two children.

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent

Officer i/c Special Branch.

JL
D.G. (Crime)
Information.
（印：MERRILL / FEB 4. / CRIME BRANCH）
M. Greene
File JL
O. i/c Sp. Br.
FEB 3 1933

档案编号 4461
特别分部 273
报告
日期：1933年2月3日。

主题（全称）附剪报一份

由谭绍良警司呈报 经罗伯特森（Tho Robertson）警司转呈

据来自南京的情报，
《字林西报》（China Times，上海）驻南京记者王维三（Wang Wei San，音译）于1月31日下午4时在南京明陵附近某处被谋杀。据一名目击者称，两名凶手均身着西装，年龄约20岁，看似学生。作案动机尚不清楚。南京当局将为缉拿凶手提供赏金。

死者为著名记者，国民党老党员，曾在各报社任职二十年。死者籍贯安徽，享年52岁。遗有寡妇及子女二人。

谭绍良
警司

特别分部主管警官。

JL
D.G.（刑事科）
情报。
（印章：MERRILL / 2月4日 / 刑事科）
M. Greene

THE CHINA PRESS. THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 2. 1933

Nanking Press
Corps Stirred
By Wang Case

Protection Petition
May Follow Killing
Of "China Times" Man

NANKING, Feb. 1.—(Reuters)—
Very keen interest has been aroused
in the Chinese capital over yester-
day's cold-blooded murder of Mr.
Wang Wei-san, the Nanking corres-
pondent of the China Times, a
Shanghai daily, who was "taken for
a ride" by two unknown men, who
shot him to death in the "Square
Park," a famous spot near the
Ming Tombs.
Rumors are flourishing today
concerning the circumstances lead-
ing to his death.
This morning at 9 o'clock the
local offices of the China Times re-
ceived a telephone call, alleged to
be from the police headquarters,
stating that two suspects had been
arrested by gendarmes stationed at
"Square Park" but the gendarmes
headquarters upon being called up
denied the report.
Mr. Wang's body is still lying at the
spot where he met his tragic death,
awaiting the arrival of his wife, who
left Wushih this morning.
The local correspondents of the
Shanghai Chinese papers are meet-
ing this afternoon to discuss the
matter, and it is expected that a
very strong petition will be lodged
with the government asking pro-
tection for journalists.
Besides pushing their investiga-
tions in order to find out the truth
about the murder, the local cor-
respondents are also raising funds
for Mr. Wang's family, who are
left in desperate financial circum-
stances.

Supt. Ian,
Please ascertain the motives
of the murder of Mr Wang

《大美晚报》（THE CHINA PRESS）。1933年2月2日，星期四

南京记者团
因王氏案件
而震动

《字林西报》记者
遇害后或随之发起
保护请愿

南京，2月1日。（路透社电）—
昨日，上海日报《字林西报》驻南京记者王维三先生遭冷血谋杀，此事在中国首都激起极大关注。王记者被两名不明身份男子“带出兜风”，在明陵附近的著名景点“方公园”（Square Park，音译）被枪杀身亡。
今天，关于导致其死亡情况的谣言四起。
今天上午9时，《字林西报》当地办事处接到一通电话，声称来自警察总局，称宪兵已在“方公园”逮捕两名嫌疑人，但致电宪兵总部后，对方否认了这一报道。
王先生的遗体仍躺在其惨遭不幸的地点，等待其妻子到来，其妻已于今晨离开无锡。
上海中文报纸的驻京记者将于今天下午开会讨论此事，预计将向政府提交一份强有力的请愿书，要求保护记者。
当地记者在加紧调查以查明谋杀真相的同时，也在为王先生的家属筹集资金，其家属目前陷入极度贫困的境地。

伊恩（Ian）警司，
请查明王先生被杀的动机
[签名] 1933年2月2日
